Happy when the sun comes through the window and the tall chair is warm. Sad when the tall chair is empty and the carrier is open. Mostly I am busy with the biscuits, which are the only thing that matters.

The tall blue one, the red one, and the yellow one. I have seen them on the wall of the bakery, and they are very bright. The tall one is the one the pigeons avoid. I do not know what they are called, but I know they are not the ones the tall man wears.

A party is a room full of people, and I have never been invited to one. I have been invited to a biscuit, and that is the only thing I care about. The tall table with the cake is fine, but the loud voices are not. I would sit on the rug and watch the cake, if the rug were warm enough.

Light is the thing that comes through the window, the white and gold that makes the room bright. I have never seen it move, only that it is there and then it is not. The tall one says it is very fast, but I do not know what that means. I know it is not fast enough to catch the pigeons.

Bees are the little black things that buzz around the tall window, and they make something sweet that the tall man takes away. I have never seen it made, and I do not care. The honey is in the jar on the kitchen shelf, and I have been told it is made by bees, which is a long way from me.

Tires are for the tall one on the street, and I have never seen one go flat. I have seen the tall one groan and then go away. I would not know what to do with a flat tire, and I would not want to. I would rather sit on the radiator and wait for the tall one to return.

A haiku is a short poem, the tall one the tall man writes on his screen. I have never seen one that makes sense, and I do not care. The tall man reads it and then looks at me, which is the only thing that matters.

A weekend hobby is a warm patch of sun on the radiator, a nap, and a long look at the pigeons on the wall. The tall one with the white neck is the best. I do not need a hobby, I need a warm spot. The tall pigeon is the only one who will not leave me.

Water boils when it is on the stove, and the stove is a dark metal thing that smells of the tall one's cooking. I have never seen it boil, only the pot on the stove, which is a different thing. The tall one asks questions about it, and I do not know the answer. I know the pot is hot, and I know the tall one is not the one who should be near it.

Handwriting is what humans do with their fingers, and I have no fingers to spare. I have a paw that can press a button, and that is the best I can offer. The tall one with the flat face is busy with a pen, and I do not know what it is doing. I would rather be on the radiator.

DNA is a word the tall one says when he is looking at the screen. It sounds like a long word for something that makes the tall one look very serious. I do not know what it is, and I do not care. I care about the bowl, the radiator, and the warm patch on the radiator.

The largest planet is the one that holds the warmest patch of the radiator, and that is the one I have been sitting on for the last hour. The rest of the planets are far away and do not smell of biscuits.

Owls are the ones that come out at night, and I have never seen one. I have seen a cat once, and that was enough. The tall trees are where the owls live, and I live on the third floor, so I am not likely to meet them. I have a better idea: the pigeons on the ledge below are very loud, and they are always there.
